title: Scoped bound: P112 star copy-cost drops need at least 20 trims
body:
The exact C/N root-star cost-64 theorem leaves further support trims outside its scope. This contribution answers the first-drop question raised by PR1242: **every original cost-seven P112 atom needs at least 20 total row-plus-column support deletions before its copied-information rank can fall**. The exact per-parent thresholds are 20 for 5,376 tagged pairs and 22 for 2,240. The recorded witnesses attain rank six. A frame-hit change is possible after only four deletions while the copy price remains seven; one extra trim changes neither quantity.

The proof reduces arbitrary erasures to minimum nonzero column-code weights, then uses rank factorization to handle simultaneous cuts on both factors. Both engines agree on all 7,616 tagged cost-seven parents (6,720 distinct support pairs), all 967,232 codeword cases, every threshold/witness/minimizer count and the complete code digests. The independent engine validates roots by Weyl reflections and enumerates dual functionals in independently obtained row coordinates.

Every copied-rank drop removes at least **560 constrained even-pair positions** from that atom's support. This counts support coverage, not paid repair operations or terms. Other costly terms may cover many positions together. No masked decoder assembly, favorable full supplier budget, physical admission or new kappa is claimed. Further trims of cost-eight/nine parents and other alphabets remain outside the census.

Reproduce the bounded registered package (Python 3.12, standard library only):

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-star-first-cost-drop
```

Core marker: `PASS_P112_STAR_FIRST_COST_DROP atoms=7616 codewords=967232 copy_drop=20 frame_change=4 even_loss=560`.

The complete Python 3.12.15 replay passes, including the final all-parent frame guard. Seven tests pass on Python 3.14.7 and 3.12.15: all 4,096 binary 3x4 matrices, 524,160 nonzero-matrix joint-cut cases, exact weighted/cardinality minima, archive/model/table corruption, refused overwrite and relocated optimized replay of both engines. Exact archive-to-Git pins, metadata and staged whitespace checks pass. The final theorem uses the written erasure lemmas; finite tests validate implementation and the fixed instance.

Base: `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`. Model/census source: PR1226 head `8b10989e4e45f0f9ce41004d7898a21a32f87e11`. Exact inputs, Git blobs, receipts, scope change, fresh OS seed46 and open next questions are in the scoped package. [Discussion1301](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1301) records coordination. The earlier seed46 P104 result concerns global live-line punctures; this result keeps P112 fixed and trims term supports.

Credit: Navinor (@navinor), PR1226, for the model/parent census; David Arias (@DavidAriasC), PR1236, for the exact-star assembly floor; Hanson Sun (@bbMisk), PR1242, for independent corroboration and the further-trim question; DreamingOfClouds/PR717 and retained PR968 geometric lineage. New application and census by Cinna Davis (@1337isnot1337), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in proofs, both implementations, checks and packaging. The engines are part of this same contribution and do not imply independent human review. Apache-2.0; frozen notice and license retained.
